key_insight: V-PaSS improves prediction of perovskite solar-cell performance for unfamiliar materials and device stacks by encoding physical alloy continuity and device chemistry.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help screen new absorber alloys and transport-layer combinations before committing to device fabrication.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, n-i-p or p-i-n polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: On institution-grouped tests with unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with reported error reductions of 15.7–19.0% on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Performance on chemistries beyond the 23-endpoint representation and prospective experimental validation are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
